text:
maria: HelixCorp just escalated — multiple users can't open the Billing page after today's RBAC refactor. They get a 403 in the console. Anyone seen this?
support: Ticket #4321. I repro'd with a test Helix user: GET /console/orgs/helix/billing -> 403. Happened right after roles-policy-v2 rollout at ~2233344400.
kevin: pulling audit logs now, will post the deny entry.
audit-bot: [policy_deny] ts=2233344402 user=helix.user1 action=console.billing.view policy=roles.policy.v2 condition="org.attr.features.billing_v2 == true" resource=org:helix
aj: That condition looks suspicious — we renamed a couple of org attributes in the migration. Helix historically uses org.attr.billing_enabled (boolean), not features.billing_v2.
devsec: Did the migration backfill map keys? I recall the script was meant to map billing_enabled -> features.billing_v2 for all orgs.
kevin: The migration ran but the filter was too strict. Script snippet that ran:
```
# bad pseudo
for org in query_orgs("attributes.features != null"):
  if org.attributes.billing_enabled:
    set org.attributes.features.billing_v2 = true
```
It only touched orgs that already had a features map; orgs with billing_enabled at top-level were skipped.
support: Ok that explains Helix. Quick mitigation options: 1) backfill missing attributes for affected orgs, 2) relax policy condition to accept legacy flag, 3) temporary allowlist for helix org. Which do we want?
maria: Prefer policy change first (low blast radius) + immediate backfill. We should avoid a broad allowlist.
kevin: I pushed a canary policy change to policy-service: OR the condition. New condition:
```
(org.attr.features.billing_v2 == true) || (org.attr.billing_enabled == true)
```
I deployed to canary at 2233344475.
deploy-bot: deploy started: service=policy-service env=canary commit=abc123
support: Can confirm Helix test user can now access billing on the canary policy.
kevin: Rolling to prod now.
deploy-bot: deploy complete: service=policy-service env=prod commit=abc123 duration=48s
support: Helix support rep just confirmed 6 users regained access. They've asked for root-cause and ETA for full revert to canonical attr.
maria: I'll open a follow-up to backfill attributes for all orgs missing features.billing_v2 and add a migration runbook. Also add a regression test that denies only when both flags are false.
devsec: Add an audit check too: nightly job to flag orgs with billing_enabled true but missing features.billing_v2. Also include in postmortem that attribute renames require dual-read capability for 7 days before enforcement.
aj: Filed INC-2026-112 and PR to add backfill script. I'll schedule the run overnight and monitor KMS/key usage — no KMS changes needed here, just metadata.
maria: Thanks everyone. Support to follow up with Helix with timeline. Closing incident once backfill completes and 24h of monitoring shows no regression. :white_check_mark:
kevin: leaving note in changelog and pushing a short incident summary to #postmortems.
maria: Great, assigning owners and tagging in the RCA draft.
